subject: Next steps: deployment mode preference and lift plan for FintechX
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechx.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap — deployment options and migration QA

Ben,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick follow-up items from our side to make a decision this quarter: 

1) Hosting preference: we currently route production traffic through an external LLModel API (OpenAI) with spikes to a legacy GPU pool for batch jobs. For Redwood, we want to understand trade-offs between Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC for a regulated payments workflow. Our priorities are: sub-200ms median latency for simple prompts, end-to-end SOC2-aligned auditability, and predictable per-token pricing for budgeting.

2) Migration constraints: we have ~6 months of cached KV state in our on-prem GPU cluster and a set of custom prompt templates. Can you outline what's required to lift-and-shift prompts and warm caches, and whether we can keep a hybrid mode while we migrate?

3) Procurement & timeline: Procurement wants a ballpark cost for Dedicated reserving 4x A100-class instances for steady throughput, plus any one-time integration work. They'll also need an editable contract redline.

If you can send a short plan (technical steps + responsibilities + estimated timeline + draft terms) that would help. I can bring Procurement into a short call.

Attachments: migration-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Alex Johnson
Head of AI Platform
FintechX
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap — deployment options and migration QA

Alex — really appreciate the clear priorities. High-level answers below and a proposed next step.

1) Trade-offs (short):
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, managed security posture, good for MVPs — but less control over dedicated throughput and peak isolation.
- Dedicated Capacity: predictable throughput, customer-dedicated GPU pools (recommended if you want guaranteed latency and reserved SLAs), Redwood handles autoscaling and kernel selection.
- Private VPC / On-prem: best for strict network isolation and full control of keys/audit logs; requires customer-managed infra or our on-prem package.

Recommendation: Given the regulatory needs and requirement for SOC2-level auditability with predictable latency, we typically recommend starting on Dedicated while keeping a small private gateway to access your legacy KV cache during transition. That gives predictable billing and a clear cutover plan.

2) Migration approach (summary):
- Phase 0: discovery and data/kv inventory (we map hot keys and prompts)
- Phase 1: hybrid run (route most production to Dedicated, but proxy cache hits to your GPU cluster for warm keys)
- Phase 2: bulk transfer & warm-up using controlled replay + synthetic traffic
- Phase 3: cutover and decommission

Lauren (cc'ed) will share a concise technical checklist and the warm-up tool we use. Monica will help with procurement and contract flow.

Next step: I can send a 2-page lift plan and a sample Dedicated pricing model + editable terms by EOD tomorrow. Would you like Procurement on that call?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechx.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Demo recap — deployment options and migration QA

Alex / Ben — adding the technical checklist Lauren-style (abridged):

- Inventory: list of prompt templates, model versions, average sequence length, and top-100 hot keys from your KV cache. (We received your migration-checklist.xlsx — thanks.)
- Networking: For Private VPC, we need VPC peering details and IP allowlists. For Dedicated with hybrid proxying, we'll deploy a small sidecar in your cluster to forward cache misses.
- KV warm: We provide a warm-up runner that replays historical calls at controlled QPS (configurable). Typical warm-up time for 100M tokens of hot cache: 12–24 hours on a 4-node Dedicated pool, depending on batch settings.
- Data handling: Redwood's Private and Dedicated options support customer-managed KMS; logs are exportable for SOC2 evidence.
- Rollback: Canary traffic + automatic fallback to your legacy API for the first 48 hours post-cutover.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-overview.pdf (pdf) — includes sample autoscale policy and SLA.

Technical ask from your side to size the Dedicated pool accurately:
- Target p95 tokens/sec (or expected concurrent requests)
- Typical prompt + response token distribution

Once we have that, we can provide a confident cost estimate and a two-week technical runbook for lift.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechx.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, FintechX Procurement <procurement@fintechx.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap — deployment options and migration QA

Ben / Lauren — this is helpful, thank you. Procurement is looped in — I've asked them to review the draft terms and confirm budget. Initial answers:
- We expect ~600 concurrent short prompts (avg 30 tokens in/60 tokens out) during peak trading windows.
- We'd like to start with Dedicated (4 reserved nodes) + hybrid proxy to our cluster for warm cache access. Plan is to move to full Dedicated within 8–12 weeks.

Please send the 2-page lift plan, sample pricing, and the editable contract redline. If Procurement agrees, we'll schedule a technical kickoff next week.

Attachments: procurement-terms-draft.docx (docx)

Best,
Alex Johnson
Head of AI Platform | FintechX
